title: OR-of-ranges scan filter as dense-mask ExpressionFilter
summary:
I added a fast path for EXPRESSION_FILTER in ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp; the change is in this one file). When the expression is an AND/OR tree whose leaves are BETWEENs or comparisons (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of the filtered column (BOUND_REF 0, exact type) against non-NULL constants of the same type, the selected values are first gathered into a dense array. Each node is then evaluated as a branch-free uint8 mask and ANDed/ORed together. The mask is ANDed with validity and turned into a fresh selection vector. Anything else falls back to the existing ExpressionExecutor path unchanged.

Measured: the lineitem scan in the q19.m0 profile went from 5.12s to 4.76s CPU, and total time from 0.725s to 0.670s. `bench q19` gave -9.0%, -7.5% and -11.1% in three runs; the full bench had q19 at only -2.9% because that run was noisy. The full bench geomean was -0.1%. That run showed q08 +12.5% and q17 +9.9%, but a re-run gave +0.6% and -0.2%, and q22 went from +6.3% to -1.1%. I didn't trace the plans of those templates to rule out the new path, but the re-runs say it was noise.

Correctness check: on a temp table with NULLs (DECIMAL, INTEGER, DATE, UTINYINT columns), 4 count queries matched the same predicates rewritten with casts so they fall back to the generic path. A sum with flipped constant-on-left comparisons and != matched its hand-computed value. I did not confirm that these test filters were actually pushed down as expression filters, so they may not have exercised the new path.
notes:
- In the prior run, evaluating the full 2048-row vector even when the incoming selection was sparse made q19 5% slower. Gathering the selected values first is essential.
- Full-bench noise on unrelated templates is about ±10% (q08, q17); re-run individual templates before drawing conclusions.
- The plan is re-analysed on every vector call (a tree walk plus reading a few Value constants). It's cheap for small trees. Precompiling it into ExpressionFilterState would need a header change.
- Possible follow-ups:
  - Add float/double support using DuckDB's NaN-aware comparison operators.
  - Extend to VARCHAR equality ORs.
  - The lineitem scan is still about 4.76s CPU, mostly from other filters (shipinstruct string equality, BF) and decoding.
